To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monocytes/macphages produce BMP‐ 2 which promotes osteogenic and proliferative differentiation of hBMMSCs.
monocytes/macropahges promote the osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow stromal cell in the presence of BMP‐2.

(1) human monocytes/macrophage‐produced BMP‐2 enhances the early differentiation and proliferation of human BMSCs, and (2) this effect is completely inhibited by blocking the BMP‐2 pathway with an anti‐Bmp2 antibody.

the effect of monocyte/macrophage‐derived BMP‐2 on the early osteoblastic differentiation of hBMCS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
monocyte/macropage cells have a positive effect on hBMSCs proliferation and differentiation.

(i) monocytes/macrophage‐derived factors, and in particular BMP‐2, are able to induce osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, (ii) this process is mediated through the activation of the BMP receptor‐mediated signalling pathway and (iii) the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs is enhanced when they are cultured with dexamethasonesupplemented medium.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monocytes/macropahges are a key player in the osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow stromal cell (hBMSC) in the presence dexamethasome‐supplemented media.
monocytes/macropahges produce BMP‐2 which promotes osteogenic and proliferative activity of hBMSC in the presence of Dexamethasone.
monocytes/macphages are able to induce the osteogenic differentiation of MSCs in the presence of DEX‐supplemented medium by the production of BMP‐2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction between monocytes/macrophage and osteoblasts is a two‐way communication that is mediated through the production of BMP‐2.
